plan.contextChunk: This figure is a line drawing of a graphical model laid out as a two-dimensional lattice in oblique projection, built from two kinds of nodes. Open white circles occupy the lattice sites, arranged in three receding rows of three visible sites each; within a row they are joined by horizontal edges that run past the rightmost circle to the frame edge, and between rows by short diagonal edges slanting down and to the left, which likewise continue off the lower-left corner, so the grid reads as a fragment of an unbounded array. A single vertical edge rises from each white circle to a solid gray filled circle, one gray node per site, drawn above and slightly behind its partner. Only the back row carries labels: its white circles are marked with the boldface symbols x_1, x_2, and x_3, and the gray circles directly above them y_1, y_2, and y_3. Because every gray node hangs off exactly one white node while the white nodes alone form the grid, the drawing separates per-site attachments from neighbor-to-neighbor coupling. The structure depicts a Markov random field over a spatial grid, each site carrying a state variable tied to its four lattice neighbors.

elements: 9 white open circles (hidden-state nodes) arranged in a 3x3 lattice: 3 horizontal rows receding up-right in oblique projection, 3 sites per row
horizontal edges within each row connecting the 3 white nodes and extending past the rightmost node to the frame edge
short diagonal edges between adjacent rows, slanting down-left, extending past the lower-left corner of the grid
9 gray filled circles (observation nodes), one per site, drawn directly above each white node
9 vertical edges linking each white node to its gray partner
bold labels x_1, x_2, x_3 beside the back row's three white nodes
bold labels y_1, y_2, y_3 beside the back row's three gray nodes

interactions.teaches: Clicking any white node highlights its four lattice neighbors and its own gray observation node while all other edges fade, revealing that a site's Markov blanket consists of its spatial neighbors plus its local evidence

interactions.label: Edges shown
interactions.teaches: Separating the white-node grid edges from the gray vertical links distinguishes neighbor-to-neighbor coupling from per-site observation evidence

interactions.label: Coupling strength
interactions.teaches: As coupling increases, neighboring white nodes take on increasingly similar shading while gray nodes stay fixed, showing how pairwise potentials encourage spatial smoothness across the field

demo_steps.title: Full model
demo_steps.narration: The complete MRF: white hidden-state nodes form the grid, each with one gray observation attached above it. The back row is labeled x_1..x_3 and y_1..y_3.

demo_steps.title: Hidden lattice only
demo_steps.narration: Hide the gray nodes and vertical links. Only the neighbor-to-neighbor grid of hidden states remains — the spatial coupling structure.

demo_steps.title: Observations only
demo_steps.narration: Hide the grid edges. Each gray y node hangs off exactly one white x node — per-site evidence, independent of neighbors.

demo_steps.title: Strong coupling
demo_steps.narration: Raise coupling strength. Neighboring white nodes converge to similar shades while the y nodes stay fixed — pairwise potentials smooth the field.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Oblique layout matching source: x-nodes at lattice sites (col, row) with col=0..2 along +X (screen-right, spacing 2.2 units) and row=0..2 receding along a diagonal up-right in the source image — model rows in -Z (depth, spacing 2.2) rendered by the standard oblique pose so depth edges slant down-left on screen. Front row (row 2) is bottom-left, back row (row 0, labeled x_1,x_2,x_3 left-to-right) is top-right. Each y node sits directly above its x node at +Y offset 1.4, radius 0.35 spheres (flat circles via sprites/cylinders facing camera are fine). White nodes: white fill #ffffff with black outline; gray nodes: solid #808080. Edges: black lines ~0.03 thick. Horizontal row edges extend ~1.5 units past the rightmost node; diagonal inter-row edges extend past the lower-left corner similarly. Labels in bold serif, offset up-right of their nodes. For the coupling slider: at strength s, each white node's shade interpolates from a per-site random base gray toward the mean of its neighbors' shades, iterated/smoothed by s; gray nodes keep fixed random gray shades.
interactionPlan.notes: Use flat circle sprites or camera-facing discs to preserve the line-drawing look. Highlight via emissive/color tint on the clicked node, its 4 (or fewer at borders) neighbors, and its y node; set all other edges to ~0.1 opacity. Toggle controls visibility/opacity of the two edge sets and gray nodes without destroying geometry. Recompute white-node shading reactively on slider change.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click any white x node to highlight its four neighboring x nodes and its attached gray y node; all other edges fade, making the local Markov blanket and conditional dependence structure visible.
- Toggle between hidden-state lattice, observation attachments, and full model views; white grid edges, gray vertical links, or both appear in turn, separating neighbor coupling from per-site evidence.
- Slider for coupling strength between neighboring x nodes; neighboring white nodes gradually take on similar shading while y nodes remain fixed, showing how pairwise potentials encourage spatial smoothness across the field.

authoredContext:
To capture relationships over space, a two-dimensional (2D) structure is
useful, called a Markov random field (MRF):

Two-dimensional Markov random field.

An example of how Markov random field models are applied to images is
depicted in the figure, which show a small image region and its context
in the image (the figure [a]). The figure [b] shows an MRF with each
node corresponding to a pixel of the image region. The states of an MRF
can be indicator variables of image segment membership for each pixel.
The states of a hypothetical most-probable configuration of this MRF are
shown as the color of each node in this illustration.

Fig (a) Image to be segmented and a local region of (a) marked in red. (b) Visualization of an MRF of nodes corresponding to image pixels inside the marked region, with states indicating segment membership, for a hypothetical most probable configuration.

discrepancies: White hidden nodes are rendered with a light-gray fill (0.78–0.98) even at zero coupling, while the source shows pure white fill with black outlines
Source figure has no control panel; generated adds substantial UI chrome (acceptable for interactivity but changes the look)
Observation gray nodes in the source are a uniform medium gray; generated uses varied gray shades per node
evaluation.notes: Faithful 3x3 oblique MRF lattice with correct white/gray node pairing, correct x1..x3/y1..y3 labels on the back row, and rich, conceptually accurate interactions (view modes, coupling slider, demo steps, Markov-blanket highlighting); only minor fill-shading deviations from the source.
action_items: Set white hidden nodes to pure white (or near-white) at zero coupling so the default view matches the source's white fill
Use a single uniform gray for all observation nodes to match the source's consistent shading

feedback.rationale: Scores are 4-5 across the board with no failure modes, and the remaining issues are only minor fill-shading polish — the figure is conceptually and interactively excellent.
